papers.title: HMA-GCA: Hybrid Manifold Augmentation and Gated Cross-Attention for circRNA-miRNA Interaction Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Circular RNAs (circRNAs) interact with microRNAs (miRNAs) to regulate gene expression and influence disease progression. However, traditional models tend to overlook the significant contributions of certain features when dealing with diverse sequence information, resulting in the inability to capture some deep topological structures and thus leaving room for improvement in prediction performance. Results We propose HMA-GCA, a novel framework that integrates hybrid manifold augmentation and gated cross-attention for CMI prediction. The model first constructs multi-scale descriptors by combining sequence-derived features (K-mer, CTD, Doc2Vec) and topological features (Role2Vec, node degree, neighborhood proximity). It then applies PCA for global linear projection and UMAP for local nonlinear manifold learning, enhancing feature representations while preserving intrinsic data geometry. A channel-wise gated cross-attention mechanism dynamically controls the injection of miRNA information into circRNA representations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that HMA-GCA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics.To ensure interpretability, we conducted SHAP analysis to quantify the contribution of each feature type, revealing that sequence-derived features and topological similarities are the most influential. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each module, while case studies demonstrate that top-ranked predictions are supported by literature evidence. Overall, HMA-GCA not only achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance but also provides interpretable insights into the molecular features. Availability and Implementation The source code and data are freely available at https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git . The implementation is based on Python and the required dependencies are listed in the repository
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) interact with microRNAs (miRNAs) to regulate gene expression and influence disease progression. However, traditional models tend to overlook the significant contributions of certain features when dealing with diverse sequence information, resulting in the inability to capture some deep topological structures and thus leaving room for improvement in prediction performance.

RESULTS: We propose HMA-GCA, a novel framework that integrates hybrid manifold augmentation and gated cross-attention for CMI prediction. The model first constructs multi-scale descriptors by combining sequence-derived features (K-mer, CTD, Doc2Vec) and topological features (Role2Vec, node degree, neighborhood proximity). It then applies PCA for global linear projection and UMAP for local nonlinear manifold learning, enhancing feature representations while preserving intrinsic data geometry. A channel-wise gated cross-attention mechanism dynamically controls the injection of miRNA information into circRNA representations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that HMA-GCA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics.To ensure interpretability, we conducted SHAP analysis to quantify the contribution of each feature type, revealing that sequence-derived features and topological similarities are the most influential. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each module, while case studies demonstrate that top-ranked predictions are supported by literature evidence. Overall, HMA-GCA not only achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance but also provides interpretable insights into the molecular features.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code and data are freely available at https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git. The implementation is based on Python and the required dependencies are listed in the repository.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 环状 RNA (circRNA) 与 microRNA (miRNA) 相互作用，调节基因表达并影响疾病进展。然而，传统模型在处理多样化的序列信息时往往会忽略某些特征的显着贡献，导致无法捕获一些深层拓扑结构，从而为预测性能留下了改进的空间。结果我们提出了 HMA-GCA，这是一种集成了混合流形增强和门控交叉注意力以进行 CMI 预测的新颖框架。该模型首先通过结合序列衍生特征（K-mer、CTD、Doc2Vec）和拓扑特征（Role2Vec、节点度、邻域邻近度）构建多尺度描述符。然后，它应用 PCA 进行全局线性投影，应用 UMAP 进行局部非线性流形学习，增强特征表示，同时保留内在的数据几何形状。通道方式门控交叉注意机制动态控制将 miRNA 信息注入 circRNA 表示中。对三个基准数据集的大量实验表明，HMA-GCA 在多个指标上始终优于最先进的方法。为了确保可解释性，我们进行了 SHAP 分析来量化每种特征类型的贡献，揭示了序列衍生特征和拓扑相似性最具影响力。消融研究证实了每个模块的必要性，而案例研究表明排名靠前的预测得到了文献证据的支持。总体而言，HMA-GCA 不仅实现了最先进的预测性能，而且还提供了对分子特征的可解释的见解。 可用性和实施​​源代码和数据可在 https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git 上免费获取。实现基于Python，所需的依赖项在存储库中列出

papers.title: Exploring the human brain, from molecules to networks, using siibra
papers.summary: Original data describing the complexity of the human brain are challenging to work with, as they can be large, heterogeneous and deposited in different repositories. We present siibra, an open software suite that links reference brain atlases with diverse, distributed datasets and makes both jointly explorable, analyzable and reusable

all_papers.title: HMA-GCA: Hybrid Manifold Augmentation and Gated Cross-Attention for circRNA-miRNA Interaction Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Circular RNAs (circRNAs) interact with microRNAs (miRNAs) to regulate gene expression and influence disease progression. However, traditional models tend to overlook the significant contributions of certain features when dealing with diverse sequence information, resulting in the inability to capture some deep topological structures and thus leaving room for improvement in prediction performance. Results We propose HMA-GCA, a novel framework that integrates hybrid manifold augmentation and gated cross-attention for CMI prediction. The model first constructs multi-scale descriptors by combining sequence-derived features (K-mer, CTD, Doc2Vec) and topological features (Role2Vec, node degree, neighborhood proximity). It then applies PCA for global linear projection and UMAP for local nonlinear manifold learning, enhancing feature representations while preserving intrinsic data geometry. A channel-wise gated cross-attention mechanism dynamically controls the injection of miRNA information into circRNA representations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that HMA-GCA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics.To ensure interpretability, we conducted SHAP analysis to quantify the contribution of each feature type, revealing that sequence-derived features and topological similarities are the most influential. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each module, while case studies demonstrate that top-ranked predictions are supported by literature evidence. Overall, HMA-GCA not only achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance but also provides interpretable insights into the molecular features. Availability and Implementation The source code and data are freely available at https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git . The implementation is based on Python and the required dependencies are listed in the repository
all_papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) interact with microRNAs (miRNAs) to regulate gene expression and influence disease progression. However, traditional models tend to overlook the significant contributions of certain features when dealing with diverse sequence information, resulting in the inability to capture some deep topological structures and thus leaving room for improvement in prediction performance.

RESULTS: We propose HMA-GCA, a novel framework that integrates hybrid manifold augmentation and gated cross-attention for CMI prediction. The model first constructs multi-scale descriptors by combining sequence-derived features (K-mer, CTD, Doc2Vec) and topological features (Role2Vec, node degree, neighborhood proximity). It then applies PCA for global linear projection and UMAP for local nonlinear manifold learning, enhancing feature representations while preserving intrinsic data geometry. A channel-wise gated cross-attention mechanism dynamically controls the injection of miRNA information into circRNA representations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that HMA-GCA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics.To ensure interpretability, we conducted SHAP analysis to quantify the contribution of each feature type, revealing that sequence-derived features and topological similarities are the most influential. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each module, while case studies demonstrate that top-ranked predictions are supported by literature evidence. Overall, HMA-GCA not only achieves state-of-the-art predictive performance but also provides interpretable insights into the molecular features.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code and data are freely available at https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git. The implementation is based on Python and the required dependencies are listed in the repository.

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 环状 RNA (circRNA) 与 microRNA (miRNA) 相互作用，调节基因表达并影响疾病进展。
llm_highlights_zh: 然而，传统模型在处理多样化的序列信息时往往会忽略某些特征的显着贡献，导致无法捕获一些深层拓扑结构，从而为预测性能留下了改进的空间。
我们提出了 HMA-GCA，这是一种集成了混合流形增强和门控交叉注意力以进行 CMI 预测的新颖框架。
该模型首先通过结合序列衍生特征（K-mer、CTD、Doc2Vec）和拓扑特征（Role2Vec、节点度、邻域邻近度）构建多尺度描述符。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 环状 RNA (circRNA) 与 microRNA (miRNA) 相互作用，调节基因表达并影响疾病进展。然而，传统模型在处理多样化的序列信息时往往会忽略某些特征的显着贡献，导致无法捕获一些深层拓扑结构，从而为预测性能留下了改进的空间。结果我们提出了 HMA-GCA，这是一种集成了混合流形增强和门控交叉注意力以进行 CMI 预测的新颖框架。该模型首先通过结合序列衍生特征（K-mer、CTD、Doc2Vec）和拓扑特征（Role2Vec、节点度、邻域邻近度）构建多尺度描述符。然后，它应用 PCA 进行全局线性投影，应用 UMAP 进行局部非线性流形学习，增强特征表示，同时保留内在的数据几何形状。通道方式门控交叉注意机制动态控制将 miRNA 信息注入 circRNA 表示中。对三个基准数据集的大量实验表明，HMA-GCA 在多个指标上始终优于最先进的方法。为了确保可解释性，我们进行了 SHAP 分析来量化每种特征类型的贡献，揭示了序列衍生特征和拓扑相似性最具影响力。消融研究证实了每个模块的必要性，而案例研究表明排名靠前的预测得到了文献证据的支持。总体而言，HMA-GCA 不仅实现了最先进的预测性能，而且还提供了对分子特征的可解释的见解。 可用性和实施​​源代码和数据可在 https://github.com/Lixunwind/Prediction-circ-mi-by-Gate.git 上免费获取。实现基于Python，所需的依赖项在存储库中列出

all_papers.title: Exploring the human brain, from molecules to networks, using siibra
all_papers.summary: Original data describing the complexity of the human brain are challenging to work with, as they can be large, heterogeneous and deposited in different repositories. We present siibra, an open software suite that links reference brain atlases with diverse, distributed datasets and makes both jointly explorable, analyzable and reusable
